tripeaks.name: TriPeaks
tripeaks.intro: I've played this every evening since I retired. Take a card one rank above or below the one in the waste. Any suit will do. It keeps my hands busy while I think.
rules: Clear all the cards from the three peaks.
The stock and the waste are below the peaks. Take any uncovered card one rank above or below the top card in the waste. A six or an eight will go on a seven, regardless of suit.
Aces and kings wrap around. You can play an ace on a king and a king or a two on an ace.
Each card you take becomes the new top card in the waste. Build long streaks to save cards in the stock and earn more stars.
If you run out of matches, select the stock to turn over a new card.
A card in the peaks becomes available once both cards covering it are gone.
If the stock is empty and there are no moves left, the deal is lost.
Undo takes back the last move. A Joker matches any card. +5 cards adds five cards to the stock.
hints: Perhaps it's time to turn over another card.
Look for a card one rank above or below the waste.
Remember, an ace can go on a king.

pyramid.name: Pyramid
pyramid.intro: My father taught me Pyramid on Sunday afternoons after tea. Take two uncovered cards that add up to thirteen. A king is worth thirteen on its own.
rules: Clear the whole pyramid.
The ace is worth 1, the jack 11, the queen 12 and the king 13. Cards from two through ten are worth their printed number.
Remove two available cards that add up to 13, such as a queen and an ace, a jack and a two, or an eight and a five. Remove a king on its own.
A card in the pyramid is available when nothing covers it.
Select the stock to turn over a card. You can pair the top card in the waste with a card from the pyramid.
You can go through the stock three times. If you reach the end and no pairs remain, the deal is lost.
Earn more stars by using fewer passes through the stock.
Undo takes back the last move. Hint highlights a pair. +1 pass lets you go through the stock once more.
hints: Thirteen. A king goes on its own.
Try the stock. You might find a match there.
A queen needs an ace and a jack needs a two.

klondike.name: Klondike
klondike.intro: All the housewives in Greywick know this one. Detectives ought to know it too. One hurried move can leave you stuck, just as it can in an investigation.
rules: Build four foundations by suit, from ace to king.
The tableau has seven columns. The last card in each column is face up.
Build down in alternating colours. A red nine goes on a black ten, then a black eight on the red nine.
You can move an entire valid run of face-up cards if its leading card fits. Removing the last face-up card in a column reveals the card underneath.
An empty column takes a king or a run starting with a king.
Send aces to the foundations, then add the two, three and remaining cards of the same suit in order.
Select the stock to turn over a card. You can turn the waste back over and go through the stock again as often as you need.
Select a card to send it to a foundation or another column if a move is available.
Use fewer passes through the stock to earn more stars.
Undo takes back the last move. Hint shows a possible move.
hints: Is there an ace waiting for its foundation?
Try to uncover a face-down card first.
Keep the empty columns for kings.

freecell.name: FreeCell
freecell.intro: Every card is in view, just like the clues on my board. It's the order that takes some thought. Keep a free cell or two for cards you haven't found a place for yet.
rules: Build four foundations by suit, from ace to king.
All 52 cards start face up in eight columns.
Build down in alternating colours. A black jack goes on a red queen, then a red ten on the black jack.
Each of the four free cells can hold one card. You can move it back to a column or to a foundation later.
An empty column can take any card.

Select a card to move it to a foundation, a matching column or a free cell. You can move a run if you have enough empty columns and free cells. If all are occupied, you can only move one card at a time.
Start each foundation with an ace, then build up in the same suit.
Win in fewer moves to earn more stars.
Undo takes back the last move. Hint shows a possible move.
hints: Don't fill all your free cells at once.
An empty column is worth more than a free cell.

golf.name: Golf
golf.intro: Take the last card in any column if it's one rank above or below the waste. When you run out of matches, turn a card from the stock. Clear the table to win.
rules: Clear all seven columns. You can only take the exposed card at the bottom of each column.
Take a card one rank above or below the waste. Suit doesn't matter. A six or an eight will go on a seven. An ace only matches a two, and a king only matches a queen.
Select a matching card or drag it onto the waste. It becomes the new top card. Select the stock when you need a different rank.
You get one pass through the stock. Save cards in the stock and use fewer undos to earn more stars.
hints: Look at the exposed cards. You need one rank higher or lower.
If there's no match, turn over a card from the stock.

spider.name: Spider
spider.intro: Build runs of spades down from king to ace. A complete run clears itself. Before dealing another row, make sure there's a card in every column.
rules: Build eight full runs from king down to ace. All cards are spades. A complete run is removed automatically.
Move one face-up card or an unbroken descending run onto a card one rank higher. For example, you can move a nine and eight together onto a ten.
An empty column takes any face-up card or descending run. Select a run and its destination, or drag it into place. A face-down card turns over when it is uncovered.
The stock deals one card to each column. Fill empty columns first. The stock has five rows.
Complete the runs in fewer moves and use fewer undos to earn more stars.
hints: Try turning over a face-down card or joining two runs.
Build what you can before dealing another row.
